rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - authors acquired 414 leaf reflectance spectra (213 diseased, 201 healthy) with a FieldSpec 3 in PACA vineyards in August and September 2016, disease status confirmed by an inspector and PCR. Q2: Tables 6-11 and Appendix Tables A1-A3, Section 3.4 and Abstract - SDIs designed by GA feature selection reached 100% accuracy with zero FNR for individual varieties in August and September versus best SVIs of 90-98%, and the authors state SDIs performed better than complete spectra and conventional SVIs in most cases (exceptions noted: ARI better for red varieties in September, complete spectra better for some combined sets); spectra were acquired under production conditions directly in the field (Introduction, Section 2.2). Q8: Section 4 (Discussion) - the SDIs depended on infestation level and variety, no single best index for FD in all situations, indices need testing on other varieties, other environments, scales and field conditions, detection only when foliar symptoms are becoming visible, and ability to distinguish FD from Bois Noir not tested.
rows.notes: The passage claims improved detection accuracy, which is exactly what the study tests, so Q2 is yes even though the row's function is pest_control; the study reports no result on disease control or management outcomes. Q3: single method (SVM cross-validated classification of spectra); inspector/PCR confirmation only provides ground truth, not an independent estimate of index accuracy. Q4: mechanism (pigment/chlorophyll changes altering reflectance) is discussed and cited, not measured; Fig. 9 shows reflectance differences but no pigment measurements. Q5: four cultivars of one crop in one region. Q6: leaf-level measurements only. Q7: the authors note indices vary with severity and variety but state this as dependence rather than a condition; borderline. Q9: 10-fold CV mean accuracies, FNR, FPR and AUC only; no SD, CI or range.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - own field spectral measurements of 414 healthy and FD-infected grapevine leaves (four cultivars, two campaigns in 2016), classified with SVM.
rows.notes: For the crop_production function the claimed effect is avoidance of yield and fruit quality losses through better detection. The study only shows that FD-specific spectral disease indices classify healthy versus infected leaves more accurately than common SVIs (Tables 6-11); it reports no yield, fruit quality or management outcome. Detection is a precondition of the production effect, so Q2 is no and upstream is set.

notes: Full text available, including appendix tables. Leaf-level spectroradiometer study in French vineyards; results are classification accuracies from 10-fold cross-validation without dispersion measures. The two rows share the same passage; they are differentiated only by the review's function attribution (detection accuracy versus yield-loss avoidance).
